## What This Chapter Does Right

### Fragment Architecture as Breath
The chapter is structurally lighter than chapters 2-3 — a breathing passage between the dense revelations of the ledger/Kova confrontation and the plot momentum of the returning skiff. The fragment rate is exceptionally high (estimated 50%+ single-sentence paragraphs), creating a staccato, contemplative rhythm that matches the narrator's watchful, waiting emotional state.

### The Five-Grey Stack (Paragraph 3)
This is the chapter's emotional anchor and demonstrates the fingerprint's fragment-stacked parallelism at full power:
> "Grey water, grey light, grey wind off a grey sea, and the fifth grey is the one inside your chest, the one the others are only weather compared to."

The four-item parallel fragment stack drums rhythm before the final item lands the emotional punch — grief as weather, weather as grief. The universalizing "your chest" deploys the fingerprint's "the way you" rhetorical posture (addressing self through generic address). This is mood-setting through structural accumulation, not purple prose.

### Anaphora as Memory (Paragraph 4)
> "He said it every time, he said it the last time, I sat with my back to the sea."

The repetition of "he said it" creates an incantation that mimics ritual memory — the narrator's mind returning liturgically to the same beat, as she walks the same roads. The punctuation collapse (no conjunction before the final clause) makes the father's words and her rebellion collide in the same sentence. This is voice at maximum precision.

### Self-Correcting Recursion (Paragraph 8)
> "I counted them the way I always count them, which is to say I did not count them, my feet counted them"

This is the fingerprint's compressed paradox/self-correcting recursion deployed as the narrator's core cognitive move — the mind correcting itself mid-thought. The ninety-six steps refrain returns again, functioning as embodied metronome.

### Procedural Log-Rhythm (Paragraph 9)
> "Wind rising by evening. Pressure falling. Wrote it down. Drew no line."

Four fragments that read as log entries embedded in narrative. The procedural notation is clean, clipped, and functions as both voice marker and emotional register — the refusal to draw the line carrying more emotional weight than any explicit statement of grief could.

### Closing Imperative (Paragraph 10)
> "Let the night try the door."

The chapter ends on a single complete sentence — matching the fingerprint's closing pattern (short, grammatically closed, resonant). The imperative form is darkly welcoming: the narrator is neither running nor resisting. She is waiting. The open-stone grammatical balance (from "drew no line" to "let the night") creates structural symmetry — what is not closed will be tried.
